content:
Bloomberg reports that despite Apple accidentally including a demo video showcasing the Visual Intelligence feature on AirPods, the product is "still expected to launch in 2027." Here are the details.

"Product challenges still being addressed"

Earlier this week, Apple accidentally included a video demonstrating Visual Intelligence running on AirPods within the macOS 26.7 Release Candidate.

Days before the video was released, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported the following in his Power On newsletter:

For years, Apple has been developing a camera-equipped version of AirPods under the codename B798. I previously reported that the device was initially planned for release in 2026, then delayed to 2027. However, Apple has also been developing another version under the codename B790 (Apple is known internally for developing competing versions of the same product).

Given Apple's accidental inclusion of the video in macOS 26.7 RC, and with the company's iPhone launch event expected to take place early next month, the B790 device seems likely to be announced at that event.

However, Gurman now reports that Apple's "plans to sell AirPods with cameras are still expected to launch in 2027, despite a leak from the company suggesting the product might arrive sooner."

The full report reads as follows:

Finally, Gurman noted that the recent leak has further intensified the controversy surrounding the device, with some users opposing the launch of camera-equipped AirPods due to privacy concerns. However, he pointed out that these cameras will be low-resolution sensors, not designed to take photos or videos, but rather to "scan the surrounding environment and provide contextual information to the Siri digital assistant and other AI tools."

Whether this will be enough to appease those who have dubbed the product "pervertpods" (變態耳機) remains to be seen until next year.
